confirmed_defects.class: pushed-directory receipts pin the staged bytes instead of enumerating the full tree against the remote blob set
confirmed_defects.invariant: PROVINCE.md/SKILL.md: a `pushed` receipt means the artifact's content is preserved in the remote. For a directory that must hold for EVERY file in the scope. Ancestry of the introducing commit, plus a digest taken at stage time, proves the bytes did not change between stage 1 and stage 4 — it never proves they were ever pushed.

confirmed_defects.note_on_D2d: utime can move mtime backward but cannot move the inode change time, so an aged container holding a freshly rewritten descendant is distinguishable from a genuinely old one. The closure judges descendant freshness on BOTH mtime and ctime; this also closes the S15 merge-battery G2 case for the stale class.

closure.summary: One shared read-only helper pair, applied identically to all four tools; no tool re-implements another's authority.
closure.D1: `r10_index_flags_reason` reads `git ls-files -v -z` over the receipt scope. Any status letter other than `H` (lowercase assume-unchanged, `S`/`s` skip-worktree, or any other letter) refuses with the flag and path named; an unreadable index refuses as `index-unverifiable`. Every helper query emits an `#rc=<n>` sentinel record that cannot collide with a path or index entry, so a failed git/scan can never be read as 'nothing to refuse'.
closure.D2: `r10_scope_reason` enumerates the scope with `find -print0` and the resolved remote ref with `git ls-tree -r -z --full-tree <ref> -- ':(literal)<rel>'`, then compares each regular file's disk blob (`git hash-object --no-filters`) to its remote blob. Missing remote copy, byte difference, symlink, submodule and non-regular entry all refuse. It also verifies every index entry in scope still exists on disk.
closure.stale_class: A directory stale receipt additionally requires every descendant to be older than --stale-days on mtime AND ctime, so a backdated child cannot launder a fresh write through an aged container.
closure.quarantine_layering: Stage 1 gains a local flag preflight (independent of the child engine), and stage 4 re-runs the full-scope enumeration on the STAGED copy instead of trusting `dir-pin-only`; the stale class re-derives descendant age locally on the staged copy so the tool does not inherit an older engine's blind spots.
closure.census: Adds an `index-flag` verdict flag (and problem-flag status) to the existing 7-column schema; `dirty` keeps its porcelain meaning so the schema is unchanged for consumers.
closure.read_only: All helpers are read-only: ls-files, ls-tree, hash-object, find, stat. Verified: index bytes are byte-identical before/after all four tools inspect a flagged repo, and the flags remain set.

controls: D1a/D2b/D2c on the installed tools are already fail-closed refusals at the quarantine layer and are NOT counted as defects (only the verdict engines' false SAFE is).

No over-refusal: an unrelated flag or dirty file outside the receipt scope does not block a clean pushed directory; a clean pushed file stays SAFE(pushed); a fully aged stale directory stays SAFE(stale).
Live-fleet guard intact: `tools/cand-d1-quarantine.sh --hold 0 <live repo> LOG.md` exits 4 with `live-fleet-mutation-forbidden` and leaves LOG.md byte-identical.
Census schema unchanged: the live-fleet row set is byte-identical to the installed census except kotodama's growing .scratch byte count (live delta).
Read-only contract: `.git/index` bytes are unchanged and the planted flags remain set after all four tools inspect a flagged repo.
not_claimed: No live removal is authorized by this fragment; the r9 freeze (tools PATCHED-NOT-CERTIFIED) stands.
The closure does not address the other clusters' open classes (ledger semantics, hidden refs, unpushed-stale fallback, worktree owner matching).
The candidate quarantine's stage-1 flag preflight is redundant when paired with the candidate engine; it exists so the guard holds against an older engine too.
No fix was attempted for the census's `dirty` column semantics — only the new `index-flag` flag was added, to keep the row schema stable.
